test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The police had caught the thief on the day before yesterday.

options.text: The thief has been caught by the police on the day before yesterday.
The thief had been caught by the police on the day before yesterday.
The thief was being caught by the police on the day before yesterday.
The thief had caught by the police on the day before yesterday.

solution:
The correct answer is: **"The thief had been caught by the police on the day before yesterday."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past perfect tense, which is formed with "**had + past participle**" of the main verb.
 
• To convert an active sentence to a passive sentence, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the main verb is changed to its past participle form.
 
• "**The thief**" is the object of the active sentence, so it becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• "**Had caught**" is the past participle form of "catch", so it becomes "had been caught" in the passive voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: "The thief has been caught by the police on the day before yesterday," is in present perfect tense, which is not correct for a past event.
 
• **Option 3**: "The thief was being caught by the police on the day before yesterday," is in past continuous tense, which implies an ongoing action, not a completed action.
 
• **Option 4**: "The thief had caught by the police on the day before yesterday," is in the active voice and has the wrong subject-verb agreement.
